title: Use the order of operations with fractions, including brackets but not exponents (½ ÷ 9/6 × (7 − 4/5))

lesson.title: Fractions Meet Order of Operations

steps.say: You already know how to handle order of operations with decimals, and you already know how to divide fractions by flipping the second one. This little step just puts those two skills together, so brackets and fractions in the same line stop being scary.

Brackets always go first, no matter what is inside them. Seven minus four fifths: think of seven as thirty five fifths, so thirty five fifths minus four fifths is thirty one fifths, which is six and one fifth.

visual.caption: Thirty one fifths sits one fifth past six

steps.say: Now division and multiplication are equal partners, so we just work left to right. Division comes first here, so one half divided by nine sixths is one half times six ninths, which is six eighteenths, and that simplifies to one third.

visual.caption: Flipping the second fraction keeps the scale balanced

steps.say: Last move: one third times thirty one fifths. Multiply the tops to get thirty one, multiply the bottoms to get fifteen, so we land on thirty one fifteenths, which is two and one fifteenth.

visual.caption: Both sides name the same amount

steps.say: Here is the trap. If you charge straight left to right and ignore the brackets, you do one half divided by nine sixths to get one third, then times seven to get seven thirds, then minus four fifths, and you end up with twenty three fifteenths. That is a whole different number, because the subtraction inside the brackets was supposed to happen before anything touched it.

visual.caption: Ignoring the brackets leaves you short

steps.say: So remember: brackets first, then divide and multiply left to right, and never let addition or subtraction jump the queue.

lesson.answer: Brackets first, then multiply and divide left to right: the answer is 31 over 15, or two and one fifteenth.

practice.question: You are splitting a bulk bag of blueberries from the Saturday market. Work out: one third divided by four sixths, times, in brackets, five minus one half. Do the brackets first, then go left to right. Give your answer in kilograms as a mixed number.
practice.answer: Brackets: five minus one half is nine halves. Then one third divided by four sixths is one third times six quarters, which is six twelfths, or one half. Finally one half times nine halves is nine quarters, so the answer is two and one quarter kilograms.
